cadet.incident.fire-mir97.brief: There's a fire! Someone might already be hurt, and the smoke will bother everyone for a while, whatever you pick.
cadet.incident.fire-mir97.response.fight: Try to put the fire out yourself.
cadet.incident.fire-mir97.response.evacuate: Get everyone out and shut the door.
cadet.incident.depress-mir97.brief: Air is leaking out of the cabin! It'll keep leaking until you fix it.
cadet.incident.depress-mir97.response.sealModu: Shut the leaky room off completely. It stops the leak, but that room's power is gone for good.
cadet.incident.depress-mir97.response.patchHul: Patch the hole with spare parts. Costs some supplies and takes a while.
cadet.incident.o2tank-apollo13.brief: The air is getting bad and it'll keep getting worse until you do something.
cadet.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.improv: Build a fix out of spare parts. It works, but the fix isn't as good as the real thing, forever.
cadet.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.ration: Have everyone slow down and rest more, so they make less bad air. But less gets done.
cadet.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.noResp: Don't do anything about the bad air.
cadet.incident.coolant-ms22.brief: Something's wrong with the cooling and it's getting hot in here.
cadet.incident.coolant-ms22.response.shedLoad: Turn some things off to cool down. It costs some crew time and the plants don't like it.
cadet.incident.coolant-ms22.response.rideItOut: Just put up with the heat.
cadet.incident.spe-1972.brief: A big solar storm is happening right now! Everyone gets some radiation no matter what, but getting to the safe room stops it from getting worse.
cadet.incident.spe-1972.response.shelterNow: Get everyone to the safe room right now!
cadet.incident.duststorm-2018.brief: A giant dust storm is covering the solar panels! Some of the dust will stay forever, no matter what you do.
cadet.incident.duststorm-2018.response.cleanAr: Send someone outside to wipe the dust off. It works best, but costs time and a little radiation.
cadet.incident.duststorm-2018.response.shedNon: Turn off things you don't need instead of going outside. Helps a little, and it's safer.
cadet.incident.duststorm-2018.response.noRespo: Don't do anything about the dust.
cadet.incident.scrubber-iss.brief: The air cleaner just broke and won't fix itself.
cadet.incident.scrubber-iss.response.swapCartr: Put in a spare part to fix the air cleaner. It works, but it gets a little weaker every time you do this.
cadet.incident.scrubber-iss.response.manualVen: Let some of the bad air out by hand, without fixing the machine.

specialist.incident.fire-mir97.brief: A fire has broken out, echoing the 1997 Mir fire. Someone may already be hurt, and the smoke will affect the crew for a while no matter which response you choose.
specialist.incident.fire-mir97.response.fight: Fight the fire directly using the outpost's fire extinguishers.
specialist.incident.fire-mir97.response.evacuate: Evacuate the area and seal it off without fighting the fire further.
specialist.incident.depress-mir97.brief: The cabin is losing pressure through a leak, similar to the 1997 Progress collision with Mir's Spektr module. It keeps leaking until it's sealed or patched.
specialist.incident.depress-mir97.response.sealModu: Seal off the leaking module completely — stops the leak for good, but permanently cuts that module's power.
specialist.incident.depress-mir97.response.patchHul: Patch the hull using spare parts — stops the leak without losing the module, but costs spares and crew time.
specialist.incident.o2tank-apollo13.brief: CO₂ is building up faster than the scrubber can handle, as it did aboard Apollo 13's lifeboat. It keeps climbing until addressed.
specialist.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.improv: Improvise a fix for the scrubber — brings CO₂ back down, but the improvised adapter is never as good as the original hardware.
specialist.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.ration: Cut crew activity to reduce how much CO₂ and heat they produce, at the cost of crew-hours available for other work.
specialist.incident.coolant-ms22.brief: A coolant leak is letting the cabin overheat, as happened aboard Soyuz MS-22. It keeps climbing toward its peak temperature until load is shed.
specialist.incident.coolant-ms22.response.shedLoad: Shed non-critical loads to cool the cabin back down — costs crew-hours and some crop health.
specialist.incident.coolant-ms22.response.rideItOut: Ride out the heat without shedding any load.
specialist.incident.spe-1972.brief: A major solar particle event is hitting, similar to the August 1972 storm. Every crew member takes a radiation dose this hour regardless of what you choose — sheltering only protects against further exposure.
specialist.incident.spe-1972.response.shelterNow: Move all crew to the storm shelter immediately.
specialist.incident.duststorm-2018.brief: A major dust storm is obscuring the solar arrays, echoing the 2018 global storm that ended Opportunity's mission. Some of this dust will never come off, however you respond.
specialist.incident.duststorm-2018.response.cleanAr: Send a crew member out to clean the arrays — clears the most dust, but costs crew-hours and radiation dose from the EVA.
specialist.incident.duststorm-2018.response.shedNon: Shed non-essential loads instead of cleaning — a smaller improvement, but no EVA needed.
specialist.incident.duststorm-2018.response.noRespo: Leave the dust where it is.
specialist.incident.scrubber-iss.brief: The CO₂ scrubber has failed outright, a recurring problem on the real ISS's CDRA system. It will not come back on its own.
specialist.incident.scrubber-iss.response.swapCartr: Swap in a spare cartridge to bring the scrubber back online — real hardware degrades a little more each time this is done, and this is no exception.
specialist.incident.scrubber-iss.response.manualVen: Manually vent some of the excess CO₂ without fixing the scrubber itself.

commander.incident.fire-mir97.brief: Onboard fire ({analogue}). One crew injury already logged; a fixed-duration smoke-recovery fatigue tail runs regardless of response.
commander.incident.fire-mir97.response.fight: Direct suppression, drawing on the tracked extinguisher stock; reduces the injury already sustained.
commander.incident.fire-mir97.response.evacuate: Evacuate and isolate; injury stands, fire contained by isolation rather than suppression.
commander.incident.fire-mir97.response.ignore: No action — fire and injury both worsen.
commander.incident.depress-mir97.brief: Cabin depressurization ({analogue}) — modeled as choked-orifice flow; O₂ decays exponentially until addressed.
commander.incident.depress-mir97.response.sealModu: Seal the module: leak eliminated; permanent solar-array-area loss (the sealed module's own arrays).
commander.incident.depress-mir97.response.patchHul: Hull patch: leak eliminated, no capacity loss; costs thermalControl spares and crew-hours.
commander.incident.o2tank-apollo13.brief: CO₂ accumulation exceeding scrubber capacity ({analogue}); rises linearly until addressed.
commander.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.improv: Improvised adapter: reduces CO₂ toward the documented post-fix level; permanent scrubber-efficiency penalty, declared and unrecoverable.
commander.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.ration: Ration activity: reduces crew metabolic output (CO₂, heat) while active; reduces today's crew-hours budget.
commander.incident.o2tank-apollo13.response.noResp: No action — CO₂ accumulation continues unchecked.
commander.incident.coolant-ms22.brief: Coolant-loop failure ({analogue}); cabin temperature approaches its documented peak on a first-order lag until load is shed.
commander.incident.coolant-ms22.response.shedLoad: Shed load: immediate, bounded cabin-temperature correction; crop-health penalty; real crew-hours cost.
commander.incident.coolant-ms22.response.rideItOut: No action — cabin temperature continues tracking toward its peak.
commander.incident.spe-1972.brief: SPE onset ({analogue}). The initial spike dose is already applied to every crew member regardless of response; only ongoing exposure is affected by location.
commander.incident.spe-1972.response.shelterNow: Relocate all living crew to the storm shelter; reduces further transmitted dose via shielding.
commander.incident.spe-1972.response.continueOpera: No relocation — crew remain at their current shielding factor for ongoing exposure.
commander.incident.duststorm-2018.brief: Dust storm onset ({analogue}). A permanent obscuration floor is applied regardless of response; only the storm-driven spike above that floor is addressable.
commander.incident.duststorm-2018.response.cleanAr: EVA array cleaning: largest obscuration reduction; crew-hours cost plus GCR/SPE dose for the EVA duration.
commander.incident.duststorm-2018.response.shedNon: Load shedding: smaller obscuration reduction; no EVA dose; lower crew-hours cost.
commander.incident.duststorm-2018.response.noRespo: No action — obscuration remains at its post-spike level.
commander.incident.scrubber-iss.brief: CO₂ scrubber failure ({analogue}); non-self-recovering, unlike an ordinary system fault.
commander.incident.scrubber-iss.response.swapCartr: Cartridge swap: restores operational status; spares cost; permanent, stacking efficiency penalty (repeat sorbent-bed degradation).
commander.incident.scrubber-iss.response.manualVen: Manual venting: one-time CO₂ reduction; scrubber remains offline.
commander.incident.scrubber-iss.response.noRespons: No action — scrubber remains offline, CO₂ continues accumulating.
